  FINISHED AGENDA AND DRAFT MINUTES

CALL TO ORDER

Meeting called to order at 9:05 AM by Co-Chair Jamies Shuford. Quorum met at 9:05 AM. This
meeting will carry no votes, only discussion.

WELCOME AND INTRODUCTION

  • Pam Chotiswatdi walks in at 9:08am.
  • Board members and staff introduced themselves, shared pronouns, agencies, and what they
  would outlaw if they could.

ICEBREAKER ACTIVITY

ROLL CALL

Commissioners Present: Wee, Shuford, Tan, Topolewski, Washington, Brezenoff, Pezzelle,
Richert, Wilson, Martins, Chotiswatdi, Bambrick, Boyce

Also present: Jennifer Santana, Secretary, Alexa Dixson-Griggs, Community Program Specialist V,
Paul Duncan, Attendee.

REGULAR AGENDA

1.  24-53159  Recommendation to discuss the Data Presentation on CoC FY 2022.

  Suggested Action:  Discuss recommendation.

  Dalton Dorr, Homeless Services Bureau Data Analyst, presented
  • Aiko Tan walks in at 9:29am.
  • He presented data on the demands of the HSB HMIS system, utilization,
  demographics, and project type performance using last year’s numbers.

  Page 1 of 5
   LONG BEACH CONTINUUM OF CARE MINUTES
  TUESDAY, APRIL 30, 2024
  4811 AIRPORT PLAZA, LONG BEACH, CA 90815
  PACIFIC GATEWAY, 9:00 AM

• From 2022 to 2023 there was a massive jump in unique individuals visiting
  the MSC. If we were to follow the pace of current trends, it can be suggested
  that there will be more individuals visiting the MSC in 2024.
• The data being presented is useful information to know where we are at,
  however the questions that we should ask ourselves are, do we have
  enough resources to supply the newly individuals/families that are coming to
  the MSC?
• It is important to note that user input is very important to be able to provide
  the most accurate data.
• Other key highlights include: the percentage of chronically homeless
  individuals is decreasing, and the homeless population is getting older, with
  a shift towards older age groups.
• Staff shared that the press release for the 2024 Homeless Point-in-Time
  Count will be on May 8th.
• Members had various questions on the supply of homeless services versus
  the demand.
• Dalton's reply showed that data alone cannot answer those types of
  questions, data can be used to answer “how much” questions. The goal of
  the presentation is to spark conversations using data to inform but not
  resolve the issues being seen in the system.
• Members of the Board and staff discussed transitional housing and the
  numbers being represented in the Data shown.
• Member Melanie Martins shared concerns about the big reduction in
  chronically homeless individuals’ data being input into HMIS. Discussion
  around data quality ensued.
• Paul Duncan spoke on the loss of economic opportunity cost study by Doctor
  Cole Hayne that showed a direct correlation between people who struggle
  with employment and the cost of living when they become adults, will
  continue the similar struggle throughout their lives.
• Member Melanie Martins shared her experience with the dramatic increase
  in older veteran adults over the age of 62 becoming newly homeless.
  Member Aiko Tan seconded that and spoke to the lack of private healthcare
  providers that are linked to that population. People put off their medical
  needs until they become too expensive, and they are at extreme levels of
  medical care.
• Paul Duncan further explained the term multiracial as listed in the PIT Count
  data. Dalton Dorr explained the guidance from HUD for those who identify as
  multiracial, and how that term was being coded as black. Latinx is now being
  included as a racial category. Ideas are floating around to incorporate that
  multiracial identity in counting and getting their representation correct.
• Member Aiko Tan spoke on her experience during the PIT Count, and how
  she felt that there was an increase of PEH from other parts of LA County and
  Central America.
• Rapid rehousing programming is doing better and has a higher occupancy

  Page 2 of 5
   LONG BEACH CONTINUUM OF CARE MINUTES
  TUESDAY, APRIL 30, 2024
  4811 AIRPORT PLAZA, LONG BEACH, CA 90815
  PACIFIC GATEWAY, 9:00 AM

  rate.
  • Paul Duncan shared that there are discussions around occupancy rates and
  reallocation of funds for agencies not meeting their goals.
  • Permanent supportive housing programs are doing better than they did last
  year.
  • Co-Chair Jamies Shuford asks whether the city and CoC are on target. Staff
  responded that Long Beach CoC compared favorably to other CoC’s. Paul
  Duncan highlighted other notable areas in which the CoC could improve.
  They included increasing RRH and transitional and PSH programs.
  • No public comment.

2.  24-53160  Recommendation to discuss the Strategic Plan Overview.

  Suggested Action:  Discuss recommendation.

  Alexa Dixson-Griggs, the Long Beach Continuum of Care Administrative
  Coordinator, presented.
  • The 2023 LB CoC Strategic Plan form and associated activities list were
  provided.
  • Lived Experience participation through ABEL has been incorporated into our
  system and is finishing the onboarding process. The community program
  specialist who will be overseeing ABEL will start soon.
  • Member Aiko Tan asked how many members we currently have; staff
  responded, 9 currently, with 2 vacant seats.
  • ABLE will assist with performance monitoring to help bring another
  perspective of experience to the Long Beach CoC homeless services
  programming.
  • System mapping is a long-term goal to assist the plan to end homelessness
  and staff continue to collaborate with the city on this goal.
  • The staff is working on the creation of a Standard Operating Procedures
  Guidance tool for providers on policies and procedures, including allowing
  cost and expenses.
  • Staff are looking at procurement and holding discussions around what is the
  need, how to streamline the process, and putting together a procurement
  calendar.
  • Staff are proud to announce increased data abilities with the CES
  incorporation into HMIS. With the matching process now within HMIS it
  should make the process cleaner and more efficient for everyone. This
  incorporation took 4 years, but it is one of the most exciting goals to meet.
  • Co-chair Jamies Shuford commented that he is happy to see this
  achievement.
  • The staff is working on creating increased training, this will include quarterly
  training courses for agencies that have been with the CoC for less than 2
  years. The training covers the basis of what and who the CoC is and does.

  Page 3 of 5
   LONG BEACH CONTINUUM OF CARE MINUTES
  TUESDAY, APRIL 30, 2024
  4811 AIRPORT PLAZA, LONG BEACH, CA 90815
  PACIFIC GATEWAY, 9:00 AM

  • The last activity needed is advocacy, staff do not currently have much
  progress on this but are working on it. They are trying to find the best method
  to build relationships with landlords and keep them engaged with the CoC.
  With the increased need for advocacy over the next year, the subcommittee
  teams will be changed around to focus on advocacy.
  • No public comments.

3.  24-53161  Recommendation to discuss 2024 Strategic Setting for the Long Beach Continuum
  of Care.

  Suggested Action:  Discuss recommendation.

  Alexa Dixson-Griggs, the Long Beach Continuum of Care Administrative
  Coordinator, presented.
  • The presentation started with a brief brainstorm of what an ideal homeless
  services system is and used those key terms to further the discussion. Key
  terms heard were timeliness, equality, and transparency.
  • From that discussion a few main strategies rose to the top of what the
  upcoming year's focus should encompass. Knowledge, data-driven, and
  efficiency were the main focuses that were agreed upon.
  • Dalton Door commented that the term data-driven should replace data-
  informed since the CoC should use their expertise in conjunction with data
  not just let the data determine future outcomes.
  • Board members agree with Dalton. Good-quality data input allows the team
  to give good-quality data.
  • Members of the Board broke out into 4 groups to discuss Funding,
  Collaboration, policies and Procedures, and Service Provision. Each group
  reported back how they best felt these categories could be accomplished.
  • Ideas included tracking progress, providing training, and addressing staff
  burnout.
  • Exploring philanthropic support and less restrictive funding. Addressing the
  challenges with administrative rates and limited funding sources.
  • The need for more flexible funding sources was discussed by all.
  • Alexa Dixson-Griggs closed the item up since it was over time. She thanked
  the group for attending and speaking up on the points mentioned. She will
  take this information and summarize it for the Board at a later meeting.
  • No public comment.
